The error usually means your async code triggered a lazy load of a relationship (or an expired attribute) that SQLAlchemy can't run implicitly in asyncio.

**What causes it**
- Accessing an unloaded relationship, such as `user.posts`, is the most common trigger. One source explains that this error happens when you try to access a Relationship attribute (like user.posts) that was not loaded in the original query. In sync code SQLAlchemy would quietly fetch the data, but in async code it cannot pause the event loop to run a synchronous "lazy load" query. Since it can't run the query, it crashes.
- Expired attributes can also trigger it. In one SQLModel example, the fields of "hero" have expired after a commit, so accessing them will raise MissingGreenlet error.
- Calling sync ORM methods inside an async session can produce the same error. One source notes that if the session is async but you're calling sync ORM methods, you get MissingGreenlet.

**How to fix it**
- **Eager load the relationship** in the query with `selectinload` or `joinedload`. The dev.to article recommends this as the main fix: tell SQLAlchemy to fetch the related data upfront using "Eager Loading" strategies like selectinload or joinedload.
- **Use awaitable access.** The async-sqlmodel project wraps relationship fields in awaitable accessors so you write `team = await hero.awt_team` instead of `hero.team`. Using an AwaitableField with Relationship fields can resolve the issues encountered during lazy loading. In plain SQLAlchemy 2.0, the equivalent is the `AsyncAttrs` mixin with `awaitable_attrs` (from my own knowledge, not from these results; check the official docs before relying on it).
- **Avoid unintended expiry.** Setting `expire_on_commit=False` on the async session (from my own knowledge, not these results) keeps attributes loaded after commit.
- **Keep objects inside their session.** Accessing attributes after the session closes causes related errors. One source notes that if the session is already gone, you get DetachedInstanceError.

**Caveat:** The Sling Academy article ties this error to eventlet or gevent monkey patching, which is a different situation from a plain asyncio app. Don't rely on its fix unless you use those libraries. The error text can also vary; one variant reads can't call await_only() here — asyncio event loop is not accessible.

**Lazy loading in async ORM (per this 2.0.54 "legacy version" page)**

- **Loader strategies:** The page doesn't strictly require specific loaders, but it steers you toward them. Its most useful eager loader is `selectinload()`. Without `AsyncAttrs`, relationships can be declared with `lazy="raise"` so they never emit SQL implicitly. Write-only relationships are described as fully asyncio-compatible and preferred. Dynamic loaders are not compatible by default.

- **expire_on_commit:** Set `expire_on_commit=False` so attributes can be read after `commit()`. The page says that "Expiration should generally not be needed" because this setting should normally be `False` under asyncio.

- **AsyncAttrs.awaitable_attrs:** Use it to access a lazy attribute as an awaitable, e.g. `for b1 in await a1.awaitable_attrs.bs:`. It was added in 2.0.13. The mixin is added to the declarative `Base`. Relationships can also be loaded explicitly with `AsyncSession.refresh()` by naming them in `attribute_names` (added in 2.0.4).

- **Implicit IO and MissingGreenlet:** The page doesn't mention `MissingGreenlet`. It says lazy loads "will usually emit IO to the database, which will fail under asyncio as no implicit IO is allowed."

- **Version context:** The page is labeled "legacy version," release 2.0.54, dated September 15, 2026. The navigation lists 2.1 as the current release.

**What the error means:** The message comes from SQLAlchemy's internal concurrency helpers. In the library source, the exception is raised when an await-style helper runs outside the greenlet context that the sync function is executed within, so the database call can't be paused and resumed. SQLAlchemy's async support relies on a top-level greenlet set up using greenlet_spawn, and the error appears when sync code runs outside that setup.

**Most common cause (async ORM):** A developer article describes this as accessing a Relationship attribute (like user.posts) that was not loaded in the original query. Sync-style code used to trigger a lazy load silently, but in async code SQLAlchemy cannot pause the event loop to run a synchronous "lazy load" query.

**Fix for that case:** Load related objects up front with eager loading, such as "Eager Loading" strategies like selectinload or joinedload.

**Other cause (eventlet/gevent):** One guide says the error typically occurs when the eventlet or gevent monkey patching is used in an asynchronous environment but the execution has not been passed into a greenlet. Its advice is to make sure monkey patching happens before importing any other module or library that does I/O. Its other suggestion, switching to create_async_engine, applies to plain asyncio apps rather than eventlet/gevent setups.

**Version note:** In SQLAlchemy 2.0.24 and later, the await_fallback() function is deprecated and will be removed in SQLAlchemy 2.1.

## Findings: SQLAlchemy `MissingGreenlet` on 2.x

**Bottom line:** The documented cause matches your observation: an unloaded relationship is read in async code outside an awaited query, so SQLAlchemy tries implicit IO that asyncio cannot run. The documented fixes are eager loading, `AsyncAttrs.awaitable_attrs`, `lazy="raise"`, and `expire_on_commit=False`. I have not reproduced your failure, so I can't confirm the root cause or that any fix works in your app.

### Project context
- Pinned: SQLAlchemy `2.0.43`, asyncpg `0.30.0`, Python 3.12 (`requirements.txt`, `project.md`).
- `project.md` says the error occurs when reading an unloaded relationship outside the awaited query. That is the common documented trigger. Your observation is consistent with it but does not prove it.
- Adding eager loading or `awaitable_attrs` is only a candidate fix until your code is reproduced.

### Evidence
- **Official docs (2.0.54 pages, read in part):** The asyncio page says lazy loads "will usually emit IO to the database, which will fail under asyncio." It recommends `selectinload()`, `lazy="raise"`, `expire_on_commit=False`, and `AsyncAttrs.awaitable_attrs` (added in 2.0.13). Its `refresh(attribute_names=...)` is available from 2.0.4. Write-only relationships are described as asyncio-safe. Sources: [SQLAlchemy asyncio docs](https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/orm/extensions/asyncio.html).
- **Official errors page:** I could not reach the MissingGreenlet section (`xd2s`). The fetched text covered other exceptions. The error text it documents is "A call to the async DBAPI was initiated outside the greenlet spawn context." Source: [SQLAlchemy errors](https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/errors.html).
- **Community (search snippet only, not read in full):** A dev.to article, reached through an aggregator, recommends eager loading with `selectinload`/`joinedload` after a `user.posts`-style access. It also notes that expired attributes after commit can trigger the error.
